extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents) and counsel handling USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, standards, and sanctions governing practice before the USPTO in patent matters — especially signature rules, restrictions on sharing electronic filing credentials, professional conduct duties, and conditions of discipline and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of practice before the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice before the Office includes law-related services connected with presentations to the Office or its officers/employees concerning a client's rights, privileges, duties, or responsibilities under laws/regulations administered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes preparing documents in contemplation of filing, corresponding and communicating with the Office, representing a client at interviews/hearings/meetings, and advising a client concerning matters pending or contemplated to be presented before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of practice in patent matters (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice in patent matters includes preparing/prosecuting patent applications, consulting in contemplation of filing, drafting specifications or claims, drafting amendments/replies requiring written argument, appeals to the PTAB, interference/derivation/reexamination proceedings, and other patent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration authorizes performance of services reasonably necessary and incident to preparation and prosecution of patent applications or proceedings in which the practitioner is authorized to participate (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO patent signature rules (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Most correspondence requiring a person's signature must be an original handwritten signature (permanent dark ink) or a direct/indirect copy of an original; only the named signatory may sign his/her name to a patent document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions and alternatives are provided (e.g., S-signature, graphic representation when e-filed). If authenticity of a copy is questioned, the Office may require the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature format and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature is inserted between forward slashes and includes only letters and/or Arabic numerals with appropriate punctuation; the signer must insert their own S-signature with a forward slash before and after (e.g., /Mr. James T. Jones, Jr./).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner signing under specified rules must supply their registration number as part of or adjacent to the S-signature; the hash (#) may only precede the registration number; design patent practitioners must indicate 'design' adjacent to the last slash; the signer's printed/typed name must be adjacent and recognizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence submitted via the USPTO electronic filing system may be signed by a graphic representation of a handwritten signature or a graphic representation of an S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic representations are acceptable only when submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system per the rules cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only the named signatory may sign
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the USPTO patent signature rules, only the named signatory may sign his or her name to a patent document; impermissible entry of a practitioner's signature by someone else is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office treats entry of another's signature as potentially adverse to integrity of the patent system and may require sanctions; examples include termination of application proceedings for fraudulent use of signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber agreements and use of PKI/sponsored accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO subscriber agreements do not permit use of USPTO Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates by persons other than a registered practitioner's employees under the practitioner's direction and control; sponsored support staff must be the practitioner's employee, an employee of practitioner's organization, or a contractor— and must not be a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners could migrate PKI certificates to USPTO.gov accounts and sponsor support staff, but sponsorship is limited to specified categories; misuse or unauthorized sharing violates subscriber agreement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to know USPTO practice rules and Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered practitioners are expected to know the rules governing practice before the Office in patent matters and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order emphasizes that practitioners should be aware of applicable patent rules of practice and professional conduct provisions; ignorance is not an excuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must provide competent representation to a client, which includes understanding USPTO patent signature rules and USPTO patent practice rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to understand signature rules, improperly sponsoring non-eligible persons, or improperly providing electronic filing credentials can constitute a violation of competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assisting unauthorized practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not assist a person not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters; assisting includes sponsoring or providing credentials and allowing a non-registered person to prepare and file patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: providing USPTO.gov access/credentials to an unauthorized relative who then prepared filings and signed the practitioner's name constitutes assisting unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving misrepresentation, which includes allowing another person to enter the practitioner's signature on patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing or facilitating false signatures on filings is treated as misrepresentation under the Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice; examples include allowing another to sign filings, improper sponsorship or provision of electronic credentials contrary to subscriber agreements, and assisting a non-registered individual to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conduct threatens the integrity of the USPTO patent issuance process and may lead to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential disciplinary consequences (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and practice rules may lead to sanctions, including suspension from practice, probation, publication of disciplinary orders, and possibly termination of application proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites published examples and warns practitioners of the range of disciplinary measures available to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposed sanction — suspension and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the agreed disposition, the practitioner is suspended from practice before the Office for 90 days and placed on probation for 12 months from the date of an order granting reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order describes these specific sanctions as those agreed upon in the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for probation violations — Order to Show Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director in good faith believes the respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director will issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent's last address, and grant 15 days to respond; after consideration, the OED Director may request the USPTO Director to suspend the respondent for up to an additional six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets out the procedural steps (issuance, service, 15-day response window, submission to USPTO Director) and allows discrete discipline to be sought separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of reinstatement — CLE on ethics/professional responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, the respondent must provide a sworn statement attesting successful completion of two (2) hours of continuing legal education credit on ethics/professional responsibility and attach corroborating documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration/affidavit must comply with 28 U.S.C. § 1746.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of reinstatement — disclosure of documents not reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must submit a sworn statement listing each patent document (by application serial number, filing date, and document type) where the respondent was identified as practitioner of record and where the document was filed between Jan 1, 2018 and the Agreement date and was not reviewed by respondent or any other registered practitioner prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration must describe with specificity the steps taken to identify such patent documents; complies with 28 U.S.C. § 1746.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of reinstatement — disclosure of documents signed by others
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must submit a sworn statement listing each patent document (by application serial number, filing date, and document type) where respondent was the named signatory but the document was signed by someone other than respondent and filed between Jan 1, 2018 and the Agreement date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration must describe with specificity the steps taken to identify such documents; complies with 28 U.S.C. § 1746.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to applicants/owners/assignees about Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, respondent must provide a copy of the Final Order to applicants, owners, or assignees of each of the identified documents and deliver the copy by certified U.S. mail (return receipt requested) or a non-electronic delivery service that can confirm delivery or attempted delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must also submit a sworn statement attesting compliance and include copies of correspondence sent and evidence of delivery or attempted delivery (28 U.S.C. § 1746).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO.gov account disabling and account-use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to respondent; as a condition of probation respondent shall not apply for, obtain, be associated with, verify credentials for, sponsor, or attempt to sponsor any USPTO.gov account for preparing or filing documents until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent is prohibited from using or assisting others in using any USPTO.gov accounts or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents while on probation; reactivation of disabled accounts is respondent's responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation requirement with USPTO inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of probation and reinstatement, respondent must cooperate with the USPTO in any inquiry regarding allegations of unauthorized practice, violations of patent rules of practice or signature rules, show cause or sanctions orders, and other matters affecting the integrity of the patent issuance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation covers inquiries tied to documents where respondent was identified as practitioner of record and other potentially adverse matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and cause a materially consistent notice to be published in the Official Gazette describing the suspension/probation and underlying misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice summarizes the facts, the rules violated (by citation), the sanctions, and warns practitioners about harms to the integrity of the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the agreement prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings against the respondent either as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary determinations may be used to inform or escalate future discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement-specific procedural waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: By agreement, the respondent waived rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, review under § 11.57, and any other appeal or challenge to the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the stipulated settlement disposition and affects procedural remedies available to the respondent.
